subtype: Approach: help neighbours through community coordination [Action]
passage:
Madhav: After you reached the school shelter, what did you do?

Maria: Honestly? Sat on a mat for one night. Then I saw a notice: the local volunteer group needed hands. I signed up, and the ward officer gave us a list of elders living alone. We didn't wade anywhere. The officer told us which lanes were safe, and the boats went to the others. My job was carrying dal and rice packets and knocking on doors with a checklist. We ticked each name, noted who needed the health volunteer to visit, and handed the sheet back to the officer at the end of the day. At first I wanted to run to the worst lane myself. I was impatient and wanted to do something big. It turned out to be better that we worked as a group, and every name got a visit.

qa.q: What did the ward officer give the volunteers?
qa.a: The ward officer gave the volunteers a list of elders living alone.

qa.q: What was Maria feeling when wanting to run to the worst lane?
qa.a: Maria felt impatient and eager to do something big, but accepted the group plan.

qa.q: What could go wrong if volunteers each went alone, and what works better?
qa.a: Lone volunteers could end up in unsafe lanes and miss people, while working with the officer covers more homes safely.

qa.q: How might an elder living alone see the volunteers' visit?
qa.a: The elder would probably feel relieved and cared for, being checked on by someone with a list and food rather than being forgotten.

grounding: Illustrates a student joining a volunteer group and working with authorities to deliver food and check on elders after reaching safety.
